AuthConfig.description:
The `runner.auth` section: who may reach the runner, and for what.

A *password* is for a person at the UI: the login page trades it for a
session cookie, so the browser never keeps the secret. A *token* is for
machines -- the CLI, `flyball-mcp`, a script -- sent as a bearer header.
Either one turns the door on; with neither the runner is open. What a
caller with neither may do is `anonymous`: nothing, or read. Levels are
`none < read < operate`; a later scheme (several sign-ins, a part of the
rig locked) changes who gets which level, not what a level admits.

password.description: The password the login page takes: a `$scrypt$` line from `flyball password`, or the plain text.
password.title: Password

token.description: Bearer token for the CLI, MCP clients and scripts.
token.title: Token

anonymous.description: What a caller with no session and no token may do: nothing, or read (every GET and every stream).
anonymous.title: Anonymous

secret.description: The key that signs sessions; default: a key file beside the store, else one made for the process (a restart then signs everyone out).
secret.title: Secret

AuthConfig.title: AuthConfig

ClockEntry.description: How the rig's time runs. Only a rig with nothing real on it may run off wall time.

stepped.description: Time moves only when stepped; for a batch run or a test.
stepped.title: Stepped

ControllerEntry.description: A controller and how it regulates its target; keyed by the target's address in the file.

signal.description: The source signal's address (a P signal).
signal.title: Signal

feedforward.description: Maps the source's unit to the target's; the law adds to it. Omit for the setpoint itself when the units agree, else none.
feedforward.title: Feedforward

min_period_s.title: Min Period S

ControllerEntry.title: ControllerEntry

DeviceEntry.description:
The envelope of one device in the rig file: flyball's keys, the same for every driver.

`driver:` picks the driver's config model by tag; the driver's own
settings sit flat beside these keys or under `config`, and both parse to
the same thing. If `config` is present it is the whole of the driver
config and any other leftover key is an error.
DeviceEntry.title: DeviceEntry

NamespaceOverride.description:
The envelope of a namespace: label, period and the overrides of what is under it.

A namespace's own driver settings (an I²C address) are not here: the
driver declares its namespaces in its own config, typed, and the
envelope only overrides what the driver declared.
NamespaceOverride.title: NamespaceOverride

ambient.description: Where a lag rests with no input (lag, fopdt).
ambient.title: Ambient

noise.description: Gaussian noise on what is read, in the output's unit.
noise.title: Noise

Rate.description: `value` per `per`. On the wire also `{"per_minute": 2}`: one key naming the unit.
Rate.title: Rate

RunnerConfig.description:
The `runner:` section: how the process serves, not what the rig is.

Everything here is fixed for the life of the process and says nothing
about the equipment, so it may live in the rig file or in a file of its
own that layers with it. A command-line flag overrides a value here.
A path is relative to the first rig file's directory.

store.description: Sessions and versions; default <rig>.sqlite beside the file.
store.title: Store

store_dir.description: Where stores live, one per rig by name: <dir>/<name>.sqlite.
store_dir.title: Store Dir

programs.description: Program files to import; default programs/ beside the file.
programs.title: Programs

tunings.description: Control-law configs; default tunings/ beside the file.
tunings.title: Tunings

drivers.description: Driver .py files; default drivers/ beside the file.
drivers.title: Drivers

auth.description: Who may reach the runner: password, token, anonymous.

compose.description: Build up a hardware rig over the API.
compose.title: Compose

allow_save.description: Let the API write rig files: a save to a path, a sim save.
allow_save.title: Allow Save

allow_shutdown.description: Let the API stop or restart the runner.
allow_shutdown.title: Allow Shutdown

keep.description: How much the scratch record holds while nothing is recorded, in the rig's clock (`1h`, `30m`); `0` keeps none.
keep.title: Keep

keep_size.description: The most the scratch record may take on disk; the oldest goes first.
keep_size.title: Keep Size

retain.description: Delete an unpinned session this long after it ended (`30d`); `0` keeps all.
retain.title: Retain

rotate.description: Close a recording at this length and continue it in a new session (`24h`); `0` never rotates.
rotate.title: Rotate

max_store.description: Keep the store under this size by deleting the oldest data, of any kind, never pinned (`20GB`); `0` sets no cap.
max_store.title: Max Store

SignalOverride.description:
The envelope's per-signal keys: metadata to override, access to remove.

`access` names the set to keep (`"r"`); `readable`, `publishing` and
`writable` drop one flag each and take only `false` -- the driver
declares what it can honour, the file cannot add to it.
SignalOverride.title: SignalOverride

TimeUnit.description: The unit a rate is expressed per.
TimeUnit.title: TimeUnit

ModbusRegister.description:
One line of a `modbus` device's tree: where a value lives, and how it converts.

`value = raw * scale`. Every register is readable and published; `write`
also makes it writable. `input` registers are read-only on real hardware,
so `write` on one is refused here too.
ModbusRegister.title: ModbusRegister

PyMeasureSignal.description:
One line of a `pymeasure` device's tree: one property, wrapped as a signal.

A property with a setter is a demand (`RPW`: its readback is the value
last set, whether or not the property also has a getter); a
getter-only one is an output, readable on demand. `publish` streams a
getter-only one too, and needs a getter -- see
[PyMeasure][flyball.integrations.pymeasure.PyMeasure].
PyMeasureSignal.title: PyMeasureSignal

QCoDeSSignal.description:
One line of a `qcodes` device's tree: one parameter, wrapped as a signal.

A settable parameter is a demand (`RPW`: its readback is the value last
set, whether or not it can be read back from the instrument); a
gettable-only one is an output, readable on demand. `publish` streams a
gettable-only one too, and needs a getter -- see
[QCoDeS][flyball.integrations.qcodes.QCoDeS].

property.description: The parameter's name, dotted for a submodule: 'source.voltage'.
property.title: Property

QCoDeSSignal.title: QCoDeSSignal

ScpiSignal.description:
One line of a `scpi` device's tree: a query, a write template, or both.

`query` alone: an output, `[RP]`. `write`, with or without `query`: a
demand, `[RPW]` -- its readback is the value last committed. Metadata
such as range, precision and limits are not here -- they are the
envelope's `signals:` overrides (plan §1.5), which apply to any driver's
tree.

query.description: A query; the reply is this signal's value.
query.title: Query

write.description: A command with `{value}` formatted in, sent on commit.
write.title: Write

quantity.description: The quantity's own name, if it differs from the signal's.
quantity.title: Quantity

scale.description: A reply or a demand is multiplied/divided by this.
scale.title: Scale

ScpiSignal.title: ScpiSignal

DaqPort.description: A `sim_daq` signal spelled out: which port, and what it measures if the plant cannot say.

tags.description: Groupings across the tree, `{axis: name}`: `{line: dry}`.
tags.title: Tags

warn.description: The band a value is normal inside; outside it, a warning.

alarm.description: The band a value is acceptable inside; outside it, an alarm.

DaqPort.title: DaqPort

FurnaceConfig.description:
A multi-zone furnace ([Furnace][flyball.sim.furnace.Furnace]).

Ports: inputs `heaterN` (a power in W, full drive being `power_w`),
outputs `zoneN` and `sample` (temperatures in °C).
FurnaceConfig.title: FurnaceConfig

PlantConfig.description:
A plant model with one input and one output, shared by the devices that use it.

Its ports are `input` (a drive, 0 to 1 of full) and `output`, whose
quantity the `sim_daq` reading it says, since a lag may be an oven or a
pressure vessel. An unknown key is refused, so the old `kind` does not
silently mean the default model.

ambient.description: Where a lag rests with no input (lag, fopdt).
ambient.title: Ambient

noise.description: Gaussian noise on what is read, in the output's unit.
noise.title: Noise

PlantConfig.title: PlantConfig

DrivePort.description:
A `sim_drive` signal spelled out: which port, and the unit and limits it is set in.

In the default `demand: input` form the signal is declared in that unit
with those limits, so an overlay can mirror a real device's writable
signal unit for unit (`blender.humidity [W] %RH 0..100`); a demand is
mapped linearly over `limits` onto the port's 0..1 drive.

`demand: output` instead declares the signal in the plant's own output
unit -- what a `sim_daq` reading the same plant would read -- and
`commit` inverts the plant's static model to find the drive, so a
controller can hand it the setpoint directly (the `setpoint`
feedforward). `quantity`/`unit` may be omitted when the plant knows its
output (a furnace zone); `limits` may be omitted when the plant's model
has a static inverse (`Lag`, `Fopdt`; not `Integrator`) -- otherwise
both must be given.

quantity.description: What is set: 'humidity', 'power' -- or, in output mode, what the plant's output measures, if it cannot say.
quantity.title: Quantity

limits.description: Input mode: what maps onto the port's drive, `limits[0]` off, `limits[1]` full. Output mode: the deliverable span, defaulted from the plant's model if it has one.

DrivePort.title: DrivePort

board.description: A board profile: a name on the board path, or a path to the file.
